day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (~45-60 min, ~€5.15 with T-Casual card). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, then take a short stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented. Head to a nearby bar for a welcome cerveza and pintxos to unwind after the flight.

meals.lunch: N/A - on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar/restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern — look for a local 'menú del día' spot or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€10-14 for a beer, bread, and a plate of patatas bravas or bocadillo.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport (€11.35) — it will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona averages 28.9°C so pack light clothes. Keep valuables secure on the metro.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro into central Barcelona (use T-Casual card). Start the day with the Sagrada Família Guided Tour — book skip-the-line tickets in advance online (~€26-33 with tower access). Arrive early around 9:00-9:30 AM before the heat peaks. The guided tour lasts ~1.5 hours and covers Gaudí's architectural genius, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the stunning interior forest of columns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter for the Gothic Quarter Walking Tour (~€15-20 for a guided group tour, or self-guided for free). Explore the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Roman ruins of Barcino, and the narrow medieval lanes. Duck into shaded alleyways to escape the afternoon heat. Visit the free Pont del Bisbe bridge and the Plaça de Sant Jaume.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, the Gothic Quarter comes alive. Grab a pre-dinner drink at one of the terrace bars on Plaça Reial (~€3-5 for a beer). Then explore El Born neighbourhood nearby for its vibrant bar scene. Check out Bar del Pla or similar local spots. This is a great intro to Barcelona's nightlife — bars fill up after 10 PM and the energy builds toward midnight.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant or tostada con tomate at a local café near the hotel or near Sagrada Família — budget ~€3-5.
meals.lunch: La Boqueria Market Food Experience on La Rambla (~€10-15) — sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, olives, and local cheeses at market stalls. Arrive by 1 PM before it gets too crowded.
meals.dinner: El Born area — look for a set menú del día (available until ~4 PM) or evening tapas. Try Bar Celta Pulpería for affordable pulpo and tapas (~€12-16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sagrada Família tickets sell out weeks in advance in August — book online before the trip. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter cobblestones. Stay hydrated; carry a refillable water bottle (public fountains are available throughout the city).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Park Güell (free to walk the lower park; ~€10 for the Monumental Zone — book online). Arrive at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds and the heat. Admire Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the famous dragon staircase, and panoramic views over Barcelona. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring the park's architectural wonders and lush gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill from Park Güell through the Gràcia neighbourhood — one of Barcelona's most charming and local-feeling districts. Browse the boutiques and street art, visit Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Then make your way to Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on Passeig de Gràcia — admire the exteriors for free (interior entry is €25-35, optional if budget allows). The entire Manzana de la Discordia block has three stunning modernista buildings to photograph.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample district for Barcelona's famous LGBTQ+ and design-bar nightlife scene (the 'Gayxample' area). Alternatively, head back to El Born or Barceloneta beach area for sunset drinks. The beach bars (chiringuitos) are lively and affordable. After midnight, explore clubs like Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (entry ~€12-18, often includes a drink) for Barcelona's legendary nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh pastry and café amb llet at a bakery in Gràcia neighbourhood (~€3-4).
meals.lunch: Grab a bocadillo or fresh fruit from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) near Gràcia for a budget picnic in the park (~€5-7).
meals.dinner: Eixample neighbourhood — try Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for excellent tapas at reasonable prices (~€15-20). Arrive before 9 PM to avoid a long queue.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell Monumental Zone tickets must be booked online in advance. The walk from Park Güell to Gràcia is downhill and very pleasant in the morning. If clubbing, note that Barcelona clubs typically don't fill up until 1-2 AM — pace yourself!

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta and spend the morning at the beach. Arrive by 9:00-10:00 AM to claim a good spot before it gets packed (Barcelona beaches are very crowded in August). Swim in the Mediterranean, relax, and enjoy the sea breeze. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture near the W Hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Raval neighbourhood — visit the MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona) exterior plaza, a hub for skaters and street culture. Walk through the colourful streets of El Raval and visit the Mercat de Sant Antoni (a beautifully restored 19th-century market) for browsing and a cool respite. Check out the Palau Güell (another Gaudí masterpiece, entry ~€12) if budget allows — it's less crowded than other Gaudí sites.
day_by_day.evening: El Raval and Parallel avenue come alive at night. Head to Bar Marsella (one of Barcelona's oldest bars, est. 1820) in El Raval for a historic absinthe experience (~€5-7 per drink). Then explore the Parallel area for live music venues and theatre bars. For a bigger night out, Sala Apolo on Avinguda del Paral·lel hosts excellent club nights (~€12-15 entry).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a beach-side café in Barceloneta — tostada con tomate y jamón and a coffee (~€5-7).
meals.lunch: Barceloneta has many affordable chiringuitos and takeaway spots. Try a fresh bocadillo de calamares or a portion of paella from a local spot (~€8-12). Avoid the most touristy restaurants right on the beach for better value.
meals.dinner: El Raval — try Elisabets restaurant on Carrer d'Elisabets for a classic, cheap Catalan menú del día (~€10-13 for three courses with wine). Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta beach gets extremely crowded in August — go early. Watch out for pickpockets on the beach and La Rambla. Apply high-SPF sunscreen. Bar Marsella is cash only and keeps irregular hours — check before going.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular (included with T-Casual card for funicular) up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (entry ~€5) for sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona, the port, and the Mediterranean. Explore the castle's ramparts and gardens. Walk through the beautiful Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic area (free or ~€3.50 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the Poble Sec neighbourhood at the foot of Montjuïc — one of Barcelona's most up-and-coming and affordable areas. Browse the Carrer de Blai, famous for its pintxos bars where you can eat well for very little. Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (Barcelona Pavilion, ~€7) — a masterpiece of modernist architecture and a must for architecture lovers. Then stroll through the Eixample one last time to admire the grid layout and modernista buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona — return to the Gothic Quarter or El Born for a farewell tapas crawl. Visit 3-4 bars and order one or two small dishes at each (patatas bravas, croquetas, pan con tomate). End the night with a walk along La Rambla (stay alert for pickpockets) and a final drink at a rooftop bar if budget allows. Head back to the hotel and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a croissant or magdalenas from a local bakery or supermarket near the hotel (~€3-4).
meals.lunch: Carrer de Blai pintxos bars in Poble Sec — load up on pintxos at €1-2 each. Budget ~€8-12 for a very satisfying lunch with a drink.
meals.dinner: Gothic Quarter tapas crawl — budget ~€15-20 total across several bars. Try El Xampanyet in El Born for cava and anchovies, or Bar Cañete near El Raval for excellent traditional tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. The T-Casual card should have enough trips remaining for the return journey. Consider buying some local products (olive oil, canned seafood, turron) at a supermarket as affordable souvenirs. August 15 is Assumption Day — some smaller shops may still have reduced hours on nearby dates.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighborhood to get oriented. Grab a light bite near the hotel and unwind after the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: La Taberna del Gourmet or a nearby local tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern – try patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and a glass of house wine (~€20–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 evening very light. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance as arrival is after 7 PM. Sant Just Desvern is a quiet suburb; the hotel likely has a bar or restaurant on-site as a backup option. Set alarms for an early start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the L5 metro from Badal or a short taxi into central Barcelona. Arrive early (9:00 AM) for your skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Spend 2–2.5 hours marveling at the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring interior columns, and the stained-glass light show. Book tower access in advance for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration – Head uphill to Park Güell (book timed entry in advance). Explore the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the Hypostyle Room. Afterward, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighborhood – browse its bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, pop into independent boutiques, and soak up the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then head to El Born district for the Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit. Start with a golden-hour stroll along Barceloneta Beach (sunset ~20:45 in August). Then dive into El Born's vibrant bar scene – try craft cocktails at Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet for cava and pintxos.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or a bakery near Sagrada Família – croissant, café amb llet, and fresh orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: A casual restaurant in Gràcia – try Cervecería Catalana or a local menú del día (3-course set lunch with wine, ~€13–16/person)
meals.dinner: El Born tapas crawl – Bar del Pla for modern Catalan tapas or El Xampanyet for traditional pintxos and house cava (~€25–35/person)

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks around 29°C – wear light clothing, sunscreen, and carry water. Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance as they sell out weeks ahead. Metro Day Pass (~€11.35) is cost-effective for multiple trips.

day_by_day.morning: La Boqueria Market Food Experience – Head to La Rambla by 9:30 AM before the crowds peak. Spend 1.5–2 hours immersing yourself in Barcelona's legendary market: sample fresh jamón ibérico, Manchego cheese, seasonal fruit, and local olives. Chat with vendors, pick up a freshly made bocadillo, and admire the stunning iron-and-glass architecture of the market hall itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Just steps from La Boqueria, dive into the labyrinthine Gothic Quarter. Join a guided walking tour (or self-guide with a map) to discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial with its Gaudí-designed lampposts, and hidden medieval courtyards. Allow 2.5–3 hours to explore at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the famous Barcelona nightlife scene. Start with pre-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar – try the Terraza del Hotel 1898 on La Rambla or Bar Calders in Sant Antoni for a local vibe. Dinner in El Raval or Eixample, then explore the Eixample 'Gayxample' bar strip or head to a live music venue like Jamboree Jazz Club in Plaça Reial for late-night jazz or DJ sets.

meals.breakfast: Graze at La Boqueria itself – fresh fruit, a tortilla española slice, and a café solo from one of the market bars (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Gothic Quarter – try La Cova Fumada (if open) or a traditional Catalan restaurant near the Cathedral for escudella or fideuà (~€15–20/person)
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda or Parking Pizza in Eixample for a mid-range, satisfying dinner before the nightlife circuit (~€20–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded after 11 AM – arrive early for the best experience and prices. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones are uneven. Jamboree Jazz Club has shows starting around 8 PM and 10 PM – check the schedule and book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Architectural Deep Dive: Eixample Modernisme Walk – Spend the morning exploring the Eixample district's extraordinary Modernista architecture. Visit Casa Batlló (book timed entry; the Magic Nights evening show is also an option) and stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the 'Block of Discord' – Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera. Pop into the free exterior viewing of Casa Milà (La Pedrera) or book interior access. This is a paradise for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill Exploration – Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular up to the hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert. Stroll through the gardens to the Castell de Montjuïc for sweeping panoramic views over the city, port, and Mediterranean. The hilltop breeze offers welcome relief from the August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Fountain of Montjuïc Light Show – The Font Màgica puts on free light-and-music shows on Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer (check schedule; typically 21:30–22:30). Watch the spectacular display in front of the Palau Nacional, then head to the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc for dinner and drinks on lively Carrer de Blai – the pintxos street of Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café or Brunch & Cake in Eixample – avocado toast, granola bowl, and specialty coffee (~€10–15)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc from a nearby deli or the Fundació Joan Miró café – sandwiches, local cheeses, and cold drinks (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl in Poble Sec – Bar Calders, Quimet & Quimet (if open), or Bodega Sepúlveda for a festive, affordable dinner (~€15–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló and La Pedrera tickets are pricey (€25–35 each) but worth it for architecture enthusiasts – prioritize one if budget is a concern. The Magic Fountain show is completely free. Poble Sec is one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable neighborhoods – a great contrast to the tourist-heavy Gothic Quarter.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach Morning & Waterfront – Spend a leisurely final morning at Barceloneta Beach. Arrive by 9:00 AM to claim a good spot before the crowds. Take a refreshing swim in the Mediterranean, rent a paddleboard or kayak, or simply relax with a book. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and admire Frank Gehry's shimmering 'Fish' sculpture at the Port Olímpic end.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Born Cultural & Memorial Centre + Last-Minute Shopping – Visit the El Born Cultural Centre, a stunning 19th-century iron market building housing excavated ruins of the 1714 siege of Barcelona – a fascinating blend of architecture and history. Afterward, browse the boutique shops of El Born for unique souvenirs: local ceramics, design items, and artisan goods. Stop by the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, a breathtaking Gothic church beloved by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Nightlife – Celebrate your last night with a proper sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant in El Born or Eixample. After dinner, enjoy one final Barcelona nightlife experience – rooftop drinks at the Terraza del Ohla Hotel or a cocktail at Paradiso (a speakeasy-style bar behind a pastrami shop in El Born, consistently ranked among the world's best bars). End the night at your leisure before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Chiringuito (beach bar) breakfast on Barceloneta – fresh orange juice, tostada con tomate y jamón, and café con leche (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada or a seafood restaurant near the port – fresh grilled fish, gambas al ajillo, and local white wine (~€20–28/person)
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet or Espai Mescladís in El Born for a memorable farewell Catalan dinner – try the tasting menu or à la carte with local wine (~€30–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Paradiso bar gets very busy after 22:00 – arrive early or expect a queue. Keep some budget for last-minute souvenirs at El Born boutiques. The metro or a taxi back to Sant Just Desvern takes approximately 25–35 minutes from central Barcelona.

Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern (~25 min by private taxi or pre-arranged hotel transfer). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Sant Just Desvern neighborhood to decompress after the flight.

meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante El Celler de Can Roca's Barcelona-area equivalent — book a table at Moments (Mandarin Oriental Barcelona) or opt for a relaxed late dinner at a local upscale Catalan bistro near the hotel, such as Can Cortada in nearby Horta, open until 23:00. Enjoy traditional Catalan cuisine with a fine wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer for a seamless arrival. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pack light layers as August evenings can still be warm at 24–26°C.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Begin the day with a skip-the-line premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds and the midday heat. Marvel at the Nativity and Passion facades, ascend the towers for panoramic city views, and explore the museum beneath the nave. The guided tour provides deep architectural context on Gaudí's vision and the basilica's century-long construction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration: After lunch, head to Park Güell (pre-booked timed entry recommended). Explore the mosaic terraces, the iconic dragon staircase, and the Hypostyle Room. Descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood — browse its bohemian boutiques, admire the modernista architecture on Carrer de Provença, and relax in one of its shaded plazas with a cold horchata.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit: As the sun begins to set (~20:30), head to Barceloneta Beach for a golden-hour stroll along the promenade. Watch the sunset over the Mediterranean with a cocktail at a beachfront chiringuito. Then transition into the El Born district for Barcelona's premier nightlife — start with craft cocktails at Bar Paradiso (hidden speakeasy behind a paella fridge), then explore the vibrant bar scene along Carrer del Rec.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Federal Café in Sant Antoni — avocado toast, fresh juices, and specialty coffee in a stylish setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — renowned for its premium tapas, fresh seafood, and Catalan craft beers. Arrive by 13:30 to secure a table.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar and tapas restaurant with anchovy montaditos, Iberian charcuterie, and house cava. Follow with late-night pintxos at Bar del Pla nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets well in advance — August is peak season and slots sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes and carry a refillable water bottle. The metro (L2/L3) connects all key stops efficiently from Sant Just Desvern via Zona Universitària.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour: Dive into Barcelona's medieval heart with a premium private guided walking tour of the Gothic Quarter. Discover 2,000-year-old Roman walls, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards that most tourists miss. A private guide adds rich historical narrative spanning Roman Barcino to the Crown of Aragon era.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience: A short walk from the Gothic Quarter along La Rambla leads to the legendary Mercat de la Boqueria. Join a curated premium food experience — sample jamón ibérico de bellota, fresh Catalan cheeses, seasonal fruits, and artisan olive oils. Pair tastings with a glass of cava. Afterward, explore the nearby El Raval neighborhood and visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) for a cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Modernista Architecture Night Walk & Upscale Dining: As the city cools, take a self-guided or private evening walk along the Eixample grid — the Manzana de la Discordia block showcases Domènech i Montaner's Casa Lleó Morera, Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller, and Gaudí's Casa Batlló (which offers a spectacular evening 'Magic Nights' experience with immersive light shows). End the night in the Eixample's upscale cocktail bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hofmann Pastisseria in El Born — one of Barcelona's finest patisseries, with buttery croissants, pain au chocolat, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar) — book months in advance for this Michelin-starred experience. Innovative small plates reinterpreting Spanish classics in a theatrical setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar — ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants, this two-Michelin-star restaurant offers a breathtaking tasting menu by former elBulli chefs. Reserve the full tasting menu with wine pairing for an unforgettable luxury dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Disfrutar and Tickets require reservations made months in advance — confirm bookings before departure. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear breathable clothing as August afternoons can be intense. Casa Batlló Magic Nights tickets should be pre-purchased online.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Sant Pere Neighborhood: Begin with a guided tour of Domènech i Montaner's UNESCO-listed Palau de la Música Catalana — a breathtaking Art Nouveau concert hall with a stained-glass skylight ceiling and ornate ceramic sculptures. If a morning concert is scheduled, book tickets for an immersive musical experience inside this architectural masterpiece. Afterward, wander the Sant Pere neighborhood's quiet streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe: Take the Montjuïc cable car or a private car up to the hill for sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona and the port. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion (Mies van der Rohe's 1929 masterpiece of modernist architecture), the Fundació Joan Miró, and the Jardins de Laribal. The hilltop offers a welcome breeze away from the city heat. Explore the Castell de Montjuïc for historical context and Mediterranean vistas.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Parallel Avenue Nightlife: Descend from Montjuïc into the vibrant Poble Sec neighborhood — Barcelona's emerging culinary and nightlife hub. Begin with aperitivo hour on Carrer de Blai (famous for its pintxos bars). Then head to Sala Apolo or Paral·lel Avenue's live music venues for world-class performances. For a more exclusive experience, visit Opium Barcelona or Shôko beach club for late-night dancing with Mediterranean views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Caravelle in El Raval — specialty single-origin coffee, avocado toast, and freshly baked pastries in an airy, design-forward space.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quimet & Quimet in Poble Sec — a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for its creative montaditos and premium tinned seafood, paired with house vermouth.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda — an intimate wine-focused restaurant in Eixample with an exceptional natural wine list and market-driven Catalan cuisine. Alternatively, book Alkimia for a refined Michelin-starred Catalan tasting menu.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Palau de la Música concert schedule in advance — attending a live performance here is a once-in-a-lifetime architectural and musical experience. Montjuïc is best visited in the late afternoon when temperatures drop. Carry sunscreen and a hat for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Diagonal Mar & Poblenou Architecture Walk: Explore Barcelona's 22@ Innovation District in Poblenou — a fascinating urban transformation zone where industrial warehouses have been converted into cutting-edge architectural landmarks. Walk along Rambla del Poblenou, visit the Torre Glòries (Jean Nouvel's luminous tower), and explore the Diagonal Mar waterfront park. This area showcases Barcelona's contemporary architectural ambition alongside its modernista heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure, Spa & Final Shopping: Return to the hotel area for a relaxed afternoon. Indulge in a spa treatment or pool session at a luxury hotel spa (the Mandarin Oriental or Arts Barcelona offer day spa access). For shopping, head to Passeig de Gràcia for Barcelona's premier luxury boutiques — Loewe, Hermès, and local Catalan designers. Visit Vinçon or BD Barcelona Design for premium Catalan design objects as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Rooftop Dinner & Cocktails: Celebrate the final evening with a rooftop dining experience showcasing Barcelona's skyline. Book a table at La Dolce Vitetta rooftop at Hotel Arts or the rooftop bar at Ohla Barcelona for sunset cocktails with views of the Gothic Quarter spires. End the night with a final walk along La Rambla and a nightcap at Bar Marsella — Barcelona's oldest bar, operating since 1820, famous for its absinthe.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel — request a premium breakfast spread with fresh fruit, Catalan pastries, smoked salmon, and cava to start the final day in style.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — a refined seafood restaurant specializing in premium paella, fresh grilled fish, and Catalan rice dishes with Mediterranean views.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona — a two-Michelin-star restaurant with a spectacular tasting menu celebrating Mediterranean seafood and Catalan terroir, paired with an exceptional Spanish wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics for the following day — arrange a private transfer back to El Prat Airport. Pack any fragile souvenirs carefully. Enoteca Paco Pérez requires advance reservation. August 20th evenings are warm and perfect for rooftop dining — no jacket needed but a light layer for late night is recommended.
